description: Delivery scenarios every Slurp SDK must pass; README.md in this folder is the state machine they check. A runner makes a client with the default options plus `options` (the flush timer is long unless a scenario sets flushIntervalMs), a key `slurp_pk_0123456789abcdef_web_<48 hex>` and an endpoint, then runs `steps` in order. Each fetch is one request and is answered from `responses` in order, and with 200 after that. A response is { status, retryAfter?, retryAfterDateSeconds?, rejected?, track? }: status 0 is a network error; retryAfter is the Retry-After header text; retryAfterDateSeconds sends Retry-After as the HTTP date that many seconds from now; rejected is a list of 1-based line numbers answered as a 400 body {"error":"invalid records","rejected":[{"line":n,"reason":"bad record"}]}; track lists event names the runner tracks on the client while that request is still unanswered. Steps: { track: [names] } records events in order (each carries data.pad of `padBytes` characters when the scenario sets padBytes); { flush: true } flushes and, while events are pending and the client has not stopped, waits for the retry deadline and flushes again; { flushOnce: true } calls flush exactly once; { sleep: ms }; { restart: true } awaits close() and makes a new client on the same storage, and { restart: { key: "slurp_pk_..." } } does the same with that publishable key instead (the same project and source with another random part, as after a key rotation); { replace: true } calls close() without awaiting it and makes a new client on the same storage at once (what init twice does). A flush or flushOnce step may carry `expect` with any of accepted, rejected, stopped, pending (the FlushResult fields) to check before the next step. `events` is shorthand for steps [{ track: events }, { flush: true }]. After the last step the runner always does one more { flush: true } and checks scenario `expect` against that result: requests is the event names in each request the server saw, in order; accepted, rejected, stopped and pending are the final client's FlushResult (accepted and rejected count only that client instance); sameRecords means every record id that appears in more than one request has the same bytes in all of them (a retry carries the same records, not necessarily the same request bytes); minRetryGapMs is the least time between the first and second request; errorsAtLeast is the least number of onError calls; keys is the publishable key sent with each request (the Authorization bearer), in order, checked only when present. `storage` makes the client's storage adapter misbehave, and the adapter is shared by every client a scenario makes: { setItem: "throws" } makes every save throw; { delayMs: n } makes every operation complete asynchronously after n ms (optional for runners whose storage is a file). Add a scenario here when a delivery bug is found, so every SDK gets the test.

scenarios.name: everything is delivered in one request
408 is retried with the same records
429 with Retry-After 0 is retried at once with the same records
429 waits for Retry-After in seconds
503 waits for Retry-After given as an HTTP date
503 is retried with the same records
500 twice then success resends the same records each time
a network error is retried with the same records
400 without a rejected list drops the request and keeps going
400 with a rejected list drops only those lines and sends the rest at once
another 4xx drops the request
401 keeps everything queued and pauses the client
a restart with the same key after a 401 makes exactly one request and pauses again
a restart with another key for the same source delivers everything a 401 left queued
403 keeps everything queued and pauses the client
a restart with the same key after a 403 makes exactly one request and pauses again
a restart with another key for the same source delivers everything a 403 left queued
a capture while paused is queued, not sent, and goes out with a new key
a paused client sends nothing even when a capture reaches flushAt
a paused client still drops the oldest lines past maxQueue
413 splits the request, first half the larger one, and delivers every event once
413 on a single event drops only that event
413 keeps splitting until the oversized event is alone, then drops just it
a success after a 413 restores the full request size
every 2xx status is an acknowledgement
204 No Content is an acknowledgement
requests are limited by maxBatchEvents
requests are limited by maxBatchBytes (a record is 2.2 to 2.7 KB, so two fit in 6000 bytes and three do not)
a record larger than maxBatchBytes travels alone
restart replays the queue that was not acknowledged
a storage adapter that fails to save does not stop delivery, and the failure is reported
replacing a client keeps every event (init twice, slow storage)
overflow while a request is in flight drops queued lines, never the ones being sent
the flush timer is not postponed by later captures
